claims.statement: For every eligible ordinary tree T and p, if the selected sum S(T,p) is positive, then some original favorable leaf tag v and some independent (p-1)-set A of H_v meeting W_v have at least p vertices addable in H_v. Consequently, if every such marked set for every selected tag has at most p-1 addable vertices, then S(T,p)<=0.
claims.scope: Conditional necessary criterion for positive witnesses and sufficient obstruction to positivity under the stated addability bound; exact original favorable selector and original leaf-tag multiplicities; does not resolve the primary target.
claims.reason: retained: the rank/alpha domains hold, actual addable vertices in each bipartition class give the per-set capacity bound, and the marked-extension incidence count yields (p-1)S=(2a+1-3p)Q-E. Nonnegative deficits prove both implications. The standing complete-sum controls are compatible and do not establish threshold realizability or a primary resolution.

limitations: The criterion does not prove or refute the primary complete aggregate inequality.
No eligible instance with a selected tagged marked set having at least p actual addable vertices is exhibited; threshold realizability and its search usefulness remain open.
Standing K_(1,12), T_22, and T_60 controls were used as supplied bounded facts and were not replayed.
